transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly. The Justice Department is reviewing
allegations against Republican operative and Trump insider Cory Lewandowski.
They stem from his time at the Department of Homeland Security. Lewandowski served as a top
aide to DHS Secretary Kristi Noem before both were pushed out in March, as NPR's Ryan Lucas reports.
The Justice Department has opened a probe into Cory Lewandowski based on a referral from the
Department of Homeland Security Inspector General. That's according to a person familiar with the
matter speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the issue.
It was not immediately clear what specific actions prosecutors are scrutinizing, but the DHS Inspector
General had been examining allegations of financial improprieties during Lewandowski's stint at the
department. Lewandowski has faced allegations that he used his position for personal profit,
he has denied wrongdoing, his attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington. Researchers say artificial intelligence
is becoming another source of political division ahead of the November midterm elections,
and PR's Windsor Johnston reports on a new study that reveals a pattern among voters outside the
country's two major parties. The study conducted by Northeastern University surveyed more than
38,000 voters in all 50 states. Researcher David Lazar says Republicans have become more trusting
of AI companies, while Democrats have grown more skeptical. But he says independents are even less
trusting than either group. To the extent that there are any swing voters left in this country,
you know, obviously the swing voters would tend to be those independents. And if you're trying
to reach out to those swing voters, conveying distrust of AI is definitely a winner. Lazar
says AI could also become an issue in closely contested races, especially when voters connect
new data centers to concerns about rising electricity and water bills. Windsor Johnston,
NPR News. The president of El Salvador has launched a military operation in Haiti,
as NPR's Aider Peralta reports his country's forces are trying to rescue Salvadoran hostages.
The Salvadoran military announced that on Sunday four Salvadoran aviation techs were ambushed and
taken hostage by heavily armed Haitian gangs. The Salvadorans deployed helicopters, which they say
were also attacked. On Wednesday, Salvadoran President Naibukkale announced what he called
a military operation. He released a video showing armored vehicles moving through Port-au-Prince.
And he issued a warning, writing, quote, "Today's attack is nothing compared to what is coming
if we do not get all four hostages back alive." The Haitian government said recovering the
Salvadorans was an absolute priority. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack.
Aider Peralta, NPR News, Mexico City. Wall Street futures are on the downside this morning.
This is NPR News. South Korea is proposing military talks with North Korea. The Ministry
of National Defense in Seoul says the intent is to resolve disagreements about the physical border
and to prevent accidental clashes in frontline areas. The proposal comes amid North Korea's
efforts to bolster its border security by adding mines, barbed wire and fencing,
as well as anti-tank walls. South Korea says North Korean soldiers have
crossed the military demarcation line dozens of times during the fortification work.
There are reports of deaths and collapsed buildings in China's southwest region of
Tibet following last night's strong earthquake. The U.S. Geological Survey says the quake had a
magnitude of seven. Astronomers think they have a new date for when Vincent van Gogh painted his
famous canvas "The Starry Night." As NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports, the date is a month later than
previously believed. Astronomers use simulations to nail down the exact date they think "The
Starry Night" represents, July 22, 1889. The researchers from Kyung-hee University in South
Korea say the stars, the moon and the planet Venus line up in a way that suggests it was
paced on their positions in the early morning. Conventional wisdom has it "The Starry Night"
was painted in June. That's in part based on letter van Gogh himself wrote, in which
he discussed painting a new study of "The Starry Sky" around that time. The researchers say their
results are not conclusive, but they argue the date the famous painting was created should be
reconsidered in light of their analysis. The work appears in the journal Scientific Reports.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
I'm Dave Mattingly in Washington. This message comes from CURE Alzheimer's Fund.
From family to community, connections and the memories they make are everything. The hugs,
the strolls, the laughs, songs and dreams. CURE Alzheimer's Fund empowers the scientists who
dedicate their lives to curing Alzheimer's disease. Great progress has been made and the momentum is
building. There is more to do. Learn more at curealz.org. Let's keep our memories together.

topics.text: Justice Department reviews allegations against Trump insider Cory Lewandowski tied to his DHS tenure
Researchers find independent voters least trusting of AI, a factor ahead of the November midterms
El Salvador's president launches military operation in Haiti to rescue four hostages taken by gangs
South Korea proposes military talks with North Korea to resolve border disputes and prevent clashes
Magnitude 7 earthquake strikes China's Tibet region, with reports of deaths and collapsed buildings
Astronomers propose July 22, 1889 as date Van Gogh painted The Starry Night, a month later than thought
